text:
Aṅguttara-Nikāya. LXXIII 2-6

These, monks, are the ten things that are desirable, pleasing, agreeable, and rare in the world.

3. Regarding these ten things that are desirable, pleasing, agreeable, and rare in the world, monks, there are ten obstacles <note>original: "paripanthā"</note>: 

4. Laziness and lack of initiative are the obstacles to wealth. Lack of adornment and lack of grooming are the obstacles to beauty. Living in unsuitable ways is the obstacle to health. Bad friendship is the obstacle to morality. Lack of restraint of the senses is the obstacle to the holy life. Deceitfulness is the obstacle to friendship. Not practicing recitation is the obstacle to deep learning. Not listening and not asking questions are the obstacles to wisdom. Lack of application and lack of reflection are the obstacles to the Teachings <note>original: "dhammānam"</note>. Wrong conduct is the obstacle to the heavenly realms.

These, monks, are the ten obstacles to these ten things that are desirable, pleasing, agreeable, and rare in the world.

5. Regarding these ten things that are desirable, pleasing, agreeable, and rare in the world, monks, there are ten sustaining conditions <note>original: "āhārā"</note>: 

6. Diligence and initiative are the sustaining conditions for wealth. Adornment and grooming are the sustaining conditions for beauty. Living in suitable ways is the sustaining condition for health. Good friendship is the sustaining condition for morality. Restraint of the senses is the sustaining condition for the holy life. Honesty is the sustaining condition for friendship. Practicing recitation is the sustaining condition for deep learning. Listening and asking questions are the sustaining conditions for wisdom. Application and reflection are the sustaining conditions for the Teachings. Right conduct is the sustaining condition for the heavenly realms.

These, monks, are the ten sustaining conditions for these ten things that are desirable, pleasing, agreeable, and rare in the world.

<summary>This text enumerates ten desirable states and identifies the specific obstacles that hinder their attainment, followed by the corresponding sustaining conditions necessary to cultivate them.</summary>
